label: Spain wildfires, 2026 season

period.status_note: Season is open. Week 29 of a Mediterranean fire season that peaks in August.

attribution_note: The Mediterranean is the region this site uses as its control for events with no El Nino link, and this is the strongest fire anomaly in the 2026 data. Not being linked to El Nino is a finding, not a caveat.

layers.label: Burnt area, year to date
layers.estimator_note: Copernicus EFFIS, via this site's fire channel

comparison.basis: same week of prior seasons, computed by Copernicus

layers.label: Forest area affected since 1 January
layers.corroboration_note: Two independent measures of the same physical quantity, about 2 percent apart. Physical quantities converge; the money figures on this page do not. That contrast is the point of this section.

layers.label: Firefighting cost so far this year

layers.method_note: This is itself a per-hectare calculation, performed by the source rather than by us, and published as a band rather than a single figure.

companion_quantity.note: 125 simultaneous fires in under 4 hours, 14 to 15 October

layers.comparability_note: An autumn wind-driven event in Atlantic Galicia. The 2026 season is a summer event in Madrid, Avila, Toledo and Castellon: different vegetation, different exposure. Shown as a reference point, not as a scaled prediction.

uncounted.label: Restoration of burnt areas
uncounted.note: Explicitly excluded from the firefighting figure by the source itself.

uncounted.label: Tourism and farming losses
uncounted.note: Named as a concern by experts in the same reporting, with no figure attached.

uncounted.label: Insured losses
uncounted.note: See absence_meaning. Three separate mechanisms exclude this hazard and territory.

absence_meaning.note: No public estimator produces an insured-loss figure for Mediterranean wildfire. PERILS covers neither wildfire as a European peril nor Spain as a territory. Spain's Consorcio de Compensacion de Seguros does not class wildfire as an extraordinary risk. France's CatNat scheme excludes forest fire by statute. Silence here says nothing whatsoever about the size of the event.

headline_candidate.text: Four published figures for Spanish firefighting costs run from EUR 1.7 billion to EUR 7.6 billion. Every one of them is the same cost per hectare multiplied by a different burnt area.
headline_candidate.form: several sources that look like corroboration are one calculation with different denominators
headline_candidate.supporting: The parameter is EUR 10,000 to 19,000 per hectare. Spain's official annual spending on fighting fires implies about EUR 4,170.
headline_candidate._guardrail: Three of the four figures are for the 2025 season and one is for 2026, so the sentence must say firefighting costs rather than implying one event. The claim is about how the figures were constructed, which is checkable by dividing each by its own area, and it is not a claim that any of them is wrong. Organisation types are stated without any inference about the figures: if the copy leaves a reader thinking the numbers are inflated, it has done something the data does not support.
headline_candidate._status: candidate, not approved copy. Editor owns the wording.
headline_candidate._why_this_and_not_the_total: Product's view, accepted: a reader who learns that four agreeing sources can be one calculation wearing three coats can use that on every damage number they meet this year. The euro total cannot travel that far.

_no_total: There is deliberately no total field in this payload and there must never be one. The layers below are different categories and their sum measures nothing.
_shape_status: working shape, not a contract. First per-event ECON payload; built for design to build the ledger template against a real case rather than an invented one.

_hazard_channel_ref.join: geography and date range, not a shared event id

_pending_decisions: Whether TLS surfaces a single central figure derived from the analog range, with tails shown, is undecided (Kristjan, 2026-07-29). No such figure is in this payload. If adopted it would be a new layer with authorship tls_built and would need its own label.
Region-matched burnt area for Portugal Centro 2017 would resolve half the apparent per-hectare spread.
Greece 2023 Alexandroupolis, about 96,000 ha, would be a third analog if a damage figure exists.
_attribution_note: Matches the fire channel's own tag for Spain. D-042: not ENSO-linked is a finding, not an apology.

derived_figure.intended_method: Spain 2026 burnt area as a share of Spain 2025 burnt area, applied to the 2025 direct damage figure. Single analog, same country, same estimator.
derived_figure._blocked_reason: the single input is unverified and contested: Spain 2025 direct damage circulates as EUR 4.3 bn and as EUR 7.6 bn, a 1.77x spread, and neither is confirmed at primary source. The European Commission's own item states the grant and gives no damage total. A tls_built figure may not rest on an unverified input.
_inputs_needed: Spain 2025 total direct damage, confirmed at primary source, with its scope stated (full season, the August wave, or the three outbreaks the Commission names)
confirmation that the EFFIS 393,079 ha full-season figure matches that scope
derived_figure._if_unblocked: At EUR 4.3 bn over the full season the ratio gives about EUR 2.4 bn for 2026 to date; at EUR 7.6 bn it gives about EUR 4.2 bn. The choice of input moves our own figure by 1.77x, which is why it is blocked rather than estimated.

component_model._floor_note: Gaps count as zero. The total is the sum of what is counted, not an estimate of the event.

sources.estimator_note: Euronews, from the Ministry for Ecological Transition area figure
sources.organisation_type: news organisation reporting a ministry figure
sources.organisation: Euronews, from the Ministry for Ecological Transition

sources.estimator_note: Greenpeace, using National Association of Forestry Companies (Asemfo) data, for the 2025 season
sources.organisation_type: advocacy organisation, using data from an industry association
sources.organisation: Greenpeace, with National Association of Forestry Companies (Asemfo) data

sources.estimator_note: Forescat, a Spanish forestry services company, for the 2025 season

response_cost.shared_parameter_note: These three figures are one per-hectare cost applied to three different burnt areas, not three independent estimates. Forescat's EUR 19,000 per hectare is the upper bound in every case.

unreconciled.label: official Spanish spending implies a far lower rate
unreconciled.basis: annual spending on fighting and extinguishing fires in a stable period
unreconciled.note: About a quarter of the parameter above, and unexplained rather than evidence. Three candidate reasons, none verified: deployed military and civil protection may sit outside the firefighting budget line; the parameter may be a marginal rate for extreme seasons rather than an average; or it may be high. Presented as an open question, because that is what it is.
unreconciled._render_note: Never place adjacent to the parameter without the three candidate reasons. The gap alone reads as an accusation the data does not carry.

response_cost._incentive_note: Organisation type is stated as a bare fact. No inference is drawn about the figures and none is available from this data. The checkable claim is only about construction: divide each published figure by its own burnt area and the same per-hectare parameter appears. Copy that leaves a reader concluding the numbers are inflated has gone beyond what the data supports.

carbon._basis: Copernicus CAMS GFAS tonnage times the EU ETS price on a stated date. Spain 2026 is among the highest emission years in the GFAS record through end of July, behind only 2022, but a verified megatonne figure for the season is not yet held.
carbon._species_required: carbon or CO2 must be named in the field; the conversion is 44/12
carbon._conservative_note: Excludes soil carbon stock loss, which on a mature forest can be about double the above-ground biomass. The line is therefore a floor.

timber_forest._basis: hectares by forest type times published timber values; not yet built

agriculture._basis: needs a land-use overlay on the burn perimeter

built_assets._basis: structure counts not yet sourced for Spain 2026

restoration._basis: explicitly excluded by the response-cost source; no separate figure found

output_bi._basis: tourism and farming losses flagged by experts in the same reporting, unquantified

mortality._basis: no verified national death toll for Spain 2026; the 2025 analog is eight, counted

component_model._floor_total_note: One component of ten is counted. The floor is the response-cost line alone, and it is already larger than the entire estimated damage of any comparable Mediterranean fire event on record. That is the finding, and it holds precisely because the other nine are visibly empty rather than quietly assumed to be zero.

secondary_finding.text: There may never be an authoritative figure for what these fires cost. No public estimator covers wildfire in Spain at all.
secondary_finding.detail: The main European insured-loss index covers neither wildfire as a peril nor Spain as a territory. Spain's national extraordinary-risk scheme does not class wildfire as an extraordinary risk. France's equivalent scheme excludes forest fire by law.
secondary_finding._provenance: moved here from the latency map on Product's suggestion, because it is about this fire season and belongs where the readers are
